title: Post-ejaculatory Optimization and Physiology of the Seminal Vesicles: A Prospective Paired MRI/CT, Contouring and Dosimetric Pilot Study
official: Post-ejaculatory Optimization and Physiology of the Seminal Vesicles: A Prospective Paired MRI/CT, Contouring and Dosimetric Pilot Study
summary:
The purpose of this study is to measure how ejaculation changes the size, shape and position of the seminal vesicles on MRI and CT scans, and whether these changes could affect radiation treatment planning.

Participants will be aksed to not ejaculate for at least 3 days prior to the visit. On the day of the visit, participants will complete standard of care MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) and CT (Computed Tomography) scans. These scans are already used in medical care but would not normally be done more than once before receiving radiation treatment. The second set of scans CT and MRI are part of the study will occur on the same day, 30-60 minutes after you ejaculate into a provided container.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age \>18 years.
2. Prostate cancer planned for curative-intent radiotherapy.
3. Patient undergoing SOC prostate MR simulation for radiotherapy planning.
4. Has successfully ejaculated within the 30 days preceding consent.
5. Able and willing to abstain from ejaculation for at least 72 hours prior to completion of the baseline SOC MR and CT simulation imaging.
6. Able and willing to undergo masturbation-induced ejaculation for study purposes and collect the ejaculate into the provided specimen container.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Prior bilateral seminal vesiculectomy or other surgery that precludes meaningful seminal vesicle assessment.
2. Anatomical distortion or disease extent judged by the investigator to prevent reliable seminal vesicle contouring.
3. Previous TURP (transurethral resection of the prostate) or any other anatomic condition that may cause retrograde ejaculation.
4. Ongoing treatment at time of study procedures with medications known to cause retrograde ejaculation such as alpha-1 blockers (e.g. tamsulosin).
5. Active genitourinary infection or other condition in which ejaculation would be medically inappropriate or unduly uncomfortable.
6. Inability to comply with study procedures.
7. Any circumstance in which the investigator believes participation would interfere with timely clinical care.
